texts.title: The Future of Remote Work
texts.text: The pandemic accelerated a trend that was already underway: the shift toward remote work. According to recent surveys, 70% of knowledge workers now expect to work from home at least part-time after the crisis ends. Companies are realizing that remote work isn't just about flexibility—it's about productivity. Employees who work from home report higher job satisfaction and fewer distractions. However, some challenges remain. Building company culture, onboarding new employees, and maintaining team cohesion can be more difficult when everyone is distributed. The future likely involves a hybrid model, where employees split their time between home and the office.

questions.text: According to the text, what percentage of knowledge workers expect to work from home at least part-time?
What does the text suggest about the challenges of remote work?
options: B) It's impossible to build company culture
C) Maintaining team cohesion can be difficult

texts.title: Sustainable Fashion
texts.text: The fashion industry is one of the most polluting industries in the world. Textile production uses enormous quantities of water, pesticides, and creates significant carbon emissions. Additionally, the culture of 'fast fashion'—where cheap clothes are produced rapidly and discarded quickly—has led to massive amounts of textile waste. However, a growing movement toward sustainable fashion is gaining momentum. Designers are experimenting with eco-friendly materials, recycling programs, and ethical manufacturing practices. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for clothing that is produced responsibly. Though the transition will be gradual, the industry is slowly moving toward a more sustainable future.

questions.text: What is the main idea of this text?
options: A) Fashion is becoming more expensive
B) The fashion industry has environmental problems, but sustainable practices are emerging
C) Consumers don't care about environment
D) All textiles should be recycled

questions.text: According to the text, 'fast fashion' contributes to the problem by:
options: B) Creating products that last too long
C) Producing cheap clothes rapidly and discarding them quickly

texts.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
texts.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing medical diagnosis. Machine learning algorithms can now detect certain cancers more accurately than human radiologists. These systems are trained on thousands of medical images, allowing them to recognize patterns that might escape human observation. The benefits are clear: faster diagnosis, earlier treatment, and potentially better outcomes. However, AI in medicine also raises ethical concerns. Questions about data privacy, algorithm bias, and who bears responsibility for incorrect diagnoses remain unanswered. Additionally, many doctors worry about job displacement. Despite these challenges, most medical professionals agree that AI will play an increasingly important role in healthcare, complementing rather than replacing human expertise.

questions.text: What advantage of AI in medical diagnosis is mentioned in the text?
options: A) It's cheaper than human doctors
B) It can detect certain cancers more accurately
D) It eliminates the need for medical training

audio_prompts.script: One of the biggest myths about productivity is that you need to work constantly to achieve results. In fact, research shows the opposite. Our brains need rest to function optimally. Taking regular breaks actually increases productivity and creativity. Studies suggest that working in 90-minute focused blocks, followed by 15-20 minute breaks, is one of the most effective patterns. During these breaks, you should do something completely different—go for a walk, drink some water, or meditate. Many successful companies now recognize this and encourage their employees to take breaks throughout the day.

questions.question: According to the podcast, what does research show about productivity?
options: D) Long work sessions are best

prompt.scenario: Your friend is planning to travel to your country for the first time. They've asked for advice about what to do and where to go.
prompt.task: Write an email giving advice and recommendations. Include: 1) A warm greeting, 2) At least 2-3 specific recommendations, 3) Practical advice (transport, accommodation, when to visit), 4) Your reasons why they should follow your advice, 5) A friendly closing.
evaluation_criteria: Register: Appropriate tone for email to friend?

prompts.instruction: Record yourself answering: 'Tell me about a hobby or interest you have. Why do you enjoy it? How long have you been doing it?' Speak for about 2 minutes.
evaluation_criteria: Fluency: Is your speech smooth or hesitant?
Grammar: Did you use past/present correctly?
Vocabulary: Did you use descriptive words?
Coherence: Did your ideas connect logically?

prompts.instruction: Record yourself giving your opinion: 'Do you think it's better to live in a big city or a small town? Give at least 2 reasons for your view.' Speak for about 1.5 minutes.
evaluation_criteria: Does your answer directly address the question?
Do you use linking words (however, for example, moreover)?
Is your pronunciation clear enough to understand easily?
